status: Pine dispatch queue reduction measured; native admission bottleneck diagnosed; no capacity qualification
baseline: Previous uncommitted Pine dispatch/checkpoint v2, not HEAD. Native fixed-work investigation also compares HEAD adadae190d9819e611ddee7f9eca17f27a7cf86e.
changes: Synchronous Pine workers copy mutable broker state and transcript containers; borrow read-only historical rows until response serialization. Public/legacy calls retain independent deep copies.
Reuse the original default-spacing finite-number/size-checked JSON response. Fall back to original compact worker encoding near framing bound; same acceptance limits.

Transport caches exact expanded JSON lengths. Changed-subtree serialized length deltas enforce original full request size bound without re-encoding unchanged history. Only successful replies advance the host-input cache.
Move native completion IDs into the instance cache, removing a redundant clone introduced by prior screening work.
Benchmark runner accepts independently frozen before/after plugin trees; same runtime, manifest, strategy sources, recipes and full initial history.
unchanged_contract: 4 fixed-affinity Pine workers, global 16 external permits, 5s worker deadline and service budget unchanged.
Per-instance in-flight exclusion, exact committed predecessor/epoch checks, cursor/idempotency and action validation unchanged.
Complete historical bars/accounts/providers/evaluations, full checkpoint content/frequency, journal sequencing and persistence-before-publication/acknowledgement unchanged.
No changes to strategy logic, matching, fees, ledger, failed-write rollback or recovery formats.

formal_comparison.recipe: Serial ABBA, two runs/version/population, each measured 30s. Pine 1000 + 38 native liquidity bots, 64-bar full prewarm, 20s warmup, 1000ms cadence, three qualified scripts, diverse inputs and 10/15/30s horizons. Native 1000 bots, 5s warmup, 25ms cadence.
formal_comparison.aggregation: Median of per-run metrics; P95 values are not pooled. Actual decision FIFO wait is paired with worker acquisition, excludes screened skips; worker acquisition wait is a separate stage.

worker_attribution.scope: Separate one-run/version diagnostic with Python tracing in both, not pooled with formal ABBA. Candidate profile predates ASCII length-only micro optimization and transport doc clarification.

native_p95_investigation.finding: Tail orders predominantly wait for room write admission. This is present in HEAD and prior v2; not evidence of PostgreSQL saturation (load uses memory journal).

before.scope: Diagnostic only: all-run spans including warmup; per-order logging affects throughput; excludes capacity comparison.

original.scope: Diagnostic only: all-run spans including warmup; per-order logging affects throughput; excludes capacity comparison.

native_p95_investigation.interpretation: Actual market-mutating versus state-only commit mix and state size vary substantially under the same seeded async load. Aggregate per-mutation means are confounded by that mix. Native fixed work does not show a material service-cost increase. A newly introduced native P95 regression is not established; contention remains.

fixed_work.scope: 1000 native bots, 64 fixed ordered clock/waves; 64000 decisions, 20409 actions; full final market/scheduler and all journal executions. Normalizes only unordered seen_order_ids. Excludes final receipt encoding from reported elapsed time. Not asynchronous admission latency.

native_p95_investigation.negative_results: Formal native step-rate median 35.015 -> 32.327 (-7.7%), cancel P95 48.194 -> 51.359ms (+6.6%); ranges are wide. Place P95 median 52.563 -> 45.063ms is observed only, not a stable native gain.

limits: Short controlled synthetic windows, not production or long-duration qualification; no PostgreSQL capacity conclusion.
Pine closed-bar backlog improves from 108/114 to 35/48 instances at endpoints but is not zero. No no-backlog capacity claim.
Native configured 40 steps/s gate (>=38) failed in all four runs; native throughput regression/noise remains unresolved as a capacity problem.
Pine literal 1 step/s gate fails in both; configured 5% tolerance passes. Pine human place P95 has a wide 20.15-104.04ms candidate range; no stable order-latency win claim.
Native counters cover whole run including warmup/quiescence. Pine stage deltas exclude those; separate diagnostic order profiles cover whole run and incur logging overhead.
Native compiler/other-server sampling is not automatic in this driver (null in provenance); compilers were completed before loads and process inventory was checked. Pine sampling verifies both zero.
attempts_and_exclusions: Initial combined Python tests lacked private external-session runtime and failed one cache assertion; private combined run then hit the legacy exact-version guard. Final separate public legacy and private broker/incremental suites pass; both failure logs retained.

First PG start omitted explicit test port and failed to bind default port. Restarted owned test data on loopback 55443 with fsync/synchronous_commit/full_page_writes ON; fresh Rust/HTTP databases; stopped afterward.

An incorrectly selected same-name service binary started during attempted fixed-test invocation, produced no measurement and was stopped. Rebuilt and froze verified hashed Release test executables; four valid fixed cases retained.
All eight formal ABBA cases and both separate worker/native profiling runs retained; no discarded performance case.
disposition: Changes left uncommitted; task-owned benchmark/test servers, workers and PostgreSQL stopped.
